source_name: Cabinet of Ministers news — SEPA accession communications
why_relevant: Official Ukrainian framing and timing of the SEPA track ('фінансовий безвіз'), including adoption of the draft-law package (17 Dec 2025). Provides the domestic-side dates to pair with EPC-side decisions.

source_name: EU NEIGHBOURS east — enlargement/screening explainers
why_relevant: EU-funded communications platform that explains screening-to-negotiation mechanics and timelines in plain language; useful as a pointer to underlying official documents and to confirm process stages, not as an authority on obligations.

source_name: Ukrainian Center for European Policy (UCEP) — independent AA implementation monitoring
why_relevant: Independent civil-society shadow monitoring of Association Agreement implementation (multi-year reports, e.g. 2014–2022 monitoring published via KAS). Valuable as a corrective to government self-reporting on whether financial-services directives were genuinely transposed.

source_name: Interfax-Ukraine (English/Ukrainian economic wire)
why_relevant: Fastest reliable reporting of NBU/CabMin steps that only later appear in official documents (e.g. NBU finalising an EBA-equivalence bill; CabMin registering SEPA accession bills). Good early-warning layer feeding verification against primary sources.

source_name: IMF — Ukraine country page (all programme documents, Article IV, staff reports)
why_relevant: Canonical publisher of Ukraine EFF programme documents: Letter of Intent, Memorandum of Economic and Financial Policies (MEFP) with dated structural benchmarks, Technical Memorandum of Understanding, and Article IV consultation reports. The hardest dated financial-sector commitments the NBU/MoF must implement originate here.

source_name: IMF Press Releases — Ukraine EFF reviews and staff-level agreements
why_relevant: Earliest public signal that a review concluded or a staff-level agreement was reached; usually names the new/extended structural benchmarks and the disbursement, weeks before the full staff report PDF is posted.

source_name: Ministry of Finance of Ukraine — Memorandum of Economic and Financial Policies section
why_relevant: Ukrainian counterpart's own landing page for the IMF memoranda, frequently hosting both the English original PDF and an unofficial Ukrainian translation. Gives the local terminology ('структурні маяки') used by regulators and press.

source_name: Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine (kmu.gov.ua) — news on IMF memorandum publication
why_relevant: Government press service announces when the IMF publishes a memorandum text and often summarises the commitments in Ukrainian; useful as a timestamped pointer to the underlying document.

source_name: MFA of Ukraine — Cooperation with international financial institutions
why_relevant: Actor-map page enumerating the IFIs engaged with Ukraine (IMF, WB, EBRD, EIB, IFC) with links — a cheap way to enumerate the assessor/conditionality landscape and its Ukrainian official naming.

source_name: MONEYVAL — Ukraine jurisdiction page (Council of Europe)
why_relevant: Authoritative index of Ukraine's mutual evaluation report, enhanced follow-up reports, technical-compliance re-ratings and progress documents — the source of dated AML/CFT obligations landing on banks and the NBU.

source_name: rm.coe.int — Council of Europe document repository (MONEYVAL PDFs)
why_relevant: The actual file store behind MONEYVAL publications; stable deep links to evaluation and follow-up PDFs, often reachable before the HTML news item is indexed.

source_name: MONEYVAL / Council of Europe newsroom — Ukraine follow-up report announcements
why_relevant: Announcement stream giving publication dates and plenary outcomes (which re-rating requests were accepted or refused) — the trigger event for tracking new AML obligations.

source_name: FATF — Mutual evaluation of Ukraine page
why_relevant: Standard-setter's own index of Ukraine's evaluation and the FATF Recommendations against which Ukraine is measured; also the reference point for grey-list / enhanced-monitoring status questions.

source_name: State Financial Monitoring Service of Ukraine (Держфінмоніторинг / FIU) — MONEYVAL and evaluation news
why_relevant: Ukraine's FIU is the national coordinator for MONEYVAL evaluations; publishes progress reports, the National Risk Assessment methodology and results, and Ukrainian-language commentary on FATF recommendation compliance and deadlines.

source_name: European Commission / Council of the EU — Ukraine Facility pages
why_relevant: Publishes the legally adopted Ukraine Plan and its amendments, payment decisions and assessment of fulfilled indicators — the EU-side equivalent of IMF benchmark verification.

source_name: World Bank — Ukraine country/projects pages (DPO/DPL prior actions)
why_relevant: Development Policy Operations for Ukraine carry 'prior actions' — dated legal/regulatory measures, including credit-market and financial-sector ones — which function as conditionality equivalent to IMF benchmarks. Programme Documents list them explicitly.

source_name: World Bank Open Knowledge Repository
why_relevant: Full-text archive of Ukraine Program Documents, Financial Sector Assessment reports and FSAP-related outputs; supports retrospective tracking of which conditionality was actually met.

source_name: EBRD — Financial Sector Reform in Ukraine (technical cooperation / policy dialogue projects)
why_relevant: EBRD funds the NBU's Project Management Office implementing the Financial Sector Development Strategy and runs policy-dialogue projects; project pages disclose which reform workstreams are resourced and on what timetable.

source_name: EBRD Evaluation Department reports on policy dialogue in Ukraine
why_relevant: Independent evaluations candidly assess where conditionality failed and why — rare 'reveals-indirectly' material on the political economy of Ukrainian financial-sector reform.

source_name: MONEYVAL Strategy 2023-2027 — unofficial Ukrainian translation (MoF)
why_relevant: Sets the evaluation cycle and methodology Ukraine will be judged under in the next round; the Ukrainian translation is the authoritative source of local terminology used by supervised institutions.

source_name: Association of Ukrainian Banks (АУБ) — financial monitoring / MONEYVAL 2026 preparation
why_relevant: Industry-body page tracking how banks are preparing for the next MONEYVAL round; surfaces the practical compliance burden and interpretation debates that never appear in the official reports.

source_name: Фінансовий клуб (finclub.net) — IMF structural benchmark reporting
why_relevant: Specialist Ukrainian financial-sector outlet that reliably itemises new and revised IMF structural benchmarks with their dates soon after each memorandum is published — a fast, Ukrainian-language early-warning layer over the IMF PDFs.

source_name: Forbes.ua / dtkt.ua / RBC-Ukraine — IMF memorandum benchmark explainers
why_relevant: General-business Ukrainian media that enumerate the structural benchmark list and flag deadline slippage (e.g. deferrals to 2027-2028); useful corroboration and for capturing benchmark revisions between formal reviews.

source_name: NISS (Національний інститут стратегічних досліджень) — analyses of World Bank Group support to Ukraine
why_relevant: State-affiliated think tank summarising the structure and conditions of World Bank Group support — helpful for mapping which operations carry financial-sector conditions and how the Ukrainian side frames them.

source_name: PaySpace Magazine (psm7.com) — NBU tag / fintech section
why_relevant: Kyiv-based specialist fintech/payments trade magazine; runs a dedicated NBU tag that tracks draft regulations, licensing actions and enforcement against payment/finance companies, usually within hours of publication and in plain language with effective dates.

source_name: PaySpace Magazine — analytics & interviews (regulator/association voices)
why_relevant: Long-form interviews with NBU deputy governors (e.g. Oleksii Shaban) and EMA director Oleksandr Karpov where implementation timelines, interchange caps and open-banking sequencing are discussed before formal publication — a primary channel for slippage signals.

source_name: Фінансовий клуб / FinClub (finclub.net) — news feed
why_relevant: Specialist banking/finance trade outlet that reports NBU draft resolutions, consultation windows and transition periods with unusual granularity (e.g. '90 days to comply', 'comments accepted until 1 September 2026', 'applies from 1 January 2027'). Highest-value single source in this cell for deadline dating.

source_name: Mind.ua — banks section
why_relevant: Business/finance outlet with a standing banks vertical and analytical 'publications' stream; covers NBU concepts (open banking), enforcement (NovaPay fine), and year-in-review pieces that summarise which regulatory deadlines actually landed.
